A Privacy Notice is an external statement; a PMP is a comprehensive internal framework.
A PMP is only required for entities with over 1,000 employees.
The PMP must be physically signed by the National Privacy Commissioner.
items.correct_answer: A Privacy Notice is an external statement; a PMP is a comprehensive internal framework.
items.explanation: A Privacy Notice only fulfills Transparency. A PMP is the holistic, internal organizational framework encompassing policies, risk assessments, training, and continuous compliance monitoring that governs the entire enterprise.

items.question_text: A company wants to implement Data Protection Measures (Pillar 4) but hasn't conducted a Privacy Impact Assessment (Pillar 2). Why is this procedurally flawed?
options: Because Pillar 4 requires a direct API link to the NPC servers.
Because without a PIA identifying specific risks, protection measures are blind guesses.
Because Pillar 2 involves paying the mandatory government compliance taxes.
It is not flawed; the pillars can be completed in any random order.
items.correct_answer: Because without a PIA identifying specific risks, protection measures are blind guesses.
items.explanation: The 5 Pillars are logically sequenced. A PIC cannot effectively implement technical or organizational security measures (Pillar 4) without first conducting a PIA (Pillar 2) to identify where the actual data risks lie.

items.question_text: At hour 71, a DPO experiences an internet outage. They print the breach report and have a courier deliver it physically to the NPC lobby, receiving a timestamp. Is this compliant?
options: Yes, physical delivery with a timestamp represents the highest compliance standard.
No, the NPC mandates exclusive use of the DBNMS portal for breach submissions.
Yes, provided they email a digital PDF copy the following business day.
No, because motorcycle couriers are not legally authorized officers of the court.
items.correct_answer: No, the NPC mandates exclusive use of the DBNMS portal for breach submissions.
items.explanation: To streamline oversight, the NPC established the Data Breach Notification Management System (DBNMS) as the exclusive, mandatory interface for submissions. Physical or ad-hoc email deliveries are procedurally non-compliant.

items.question_text: A registered corporation implements flawless security and experiences absolutely zero incidents, breaches, or blocked attacks all year. What must they file for their ASIR?
options: They are entirely exempt from filing an ASIR for that calendar year.
They must formally submit an ASIR declaring zero incidents via the DBNMS.
They only need to send a brief email to the NPC compliance desk.
They must undergo an expensive physical audit to verify the zero incidents.
items.correct_answer: They must formally submit an ASIR declaring zero incidents via the DBNMS.
items.explanation: The Annual Security Incident Report (ASIR) is a mandatory compliance requirement for registered entities. Even if a company has a perfect record, they must formally file the report to declare zero incidents.

items.question_text: A DPO submits the preliminary 72-hour report but realizes complex forensics will take 10 more days, exceeding the 5-day deadline for the Full Breach Report. What must they do?
options: Wait silently until forensics complete, then submit the massive final report.
Proactively submit a formal written request for an extension before the 5 days expire.
Retract the preliminary notification and entirely restart the 72-hour clock.
Submit the report to the Department of Information and Communications Technology.
items.correct_answer: Proactively submit a formal written request for an extension before the 5 days expire.
items.explanation: NPC Circular 16-03 strictly requires the Full Breach Report within 5 days of the preliminary notice. If impossible, the PIC must formally request an extension from the NPC, detailing the forensic delays, before the deadline lapses.

items.question_text: A local embassy of a foreign government situated in Taguig processes visa applications containing biometric SPI of Filipino citizens. A rejected applicant files a Section 16 complaint with the NPC for unlawful denial. How must the NPC rule?
options: Assert sovereign jurisdiction under Section 6 because the applicant is a Philippine citizen.
Dismiss the complaint because diplomatic missions and consular archives are protected by international law and Vienna Convention immunities.
Order a mandatory joint investigation with the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA).
Subpoena the ambassador's chief of staff to produce the visa processing logs within 72 hours.
items.correct_answer: Dismiss the complaint because diplomatic missions and consular archives are protected by international law and Vienna Convention immunities.
items.explanation: Under international law and statutory scope principles recognized by the DPA, diplomatic premises, archives, and official embassy communications are inviolable under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, placing foreign missions outside NPC enforcement jurisdiction.

items.lesson_concept: Section 4 Exclusion for Offshore Outsourcing (Safe Harbor)
items.question_text: A Cebu-based BPO processes customer financial records solely originating from Canadian citizens on behalf of a Toronto bank. No data of Philippine residents is collected or merged. Under Section 4(e) of RA 10173, which conditions must be met for this safe harbor exemption?
options: The BPO is completely exempt from all Philippine laws and needs no local DPO.
The data must be processed strictly in accordance with Canadian privacy legislation and the terms of the service contract, while following Philippine security measure standards.
The BPO must register each Canadian customer's identity with the NPC within 30 days.
The exemption only applies if the BPO operates inside an accredited PEZA IT-Ecozone.
items.correct_answer: The data must be processed strictly in accordance with Canadian privacy legislation and the terms of the service contract, while following Philippine security measure standards.
items.explanation: Under Section 4(e) of the DPA, information originally collected from foreign jurisdictions and processed in the Philippines solely under outsourcing contracts is exempt from the DPA's substantive provisions, provided the processor complies with the foreign privacy laws, contract terms, and minimum security safeguards.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Administrative Cease and Desist Order (CDO) Powers
items.question_text: The NPC issues an ex-parte Temporary Cease and Desist Order (CDO) against a predatory online lending app for scraping user contact lists. The app developer argues that the CDO is unconstitutional without a prior formal trial court hearing. Is the developer's argument valid?
options: Yes, only a Regional Trial Court (RTC) judge possesses the constitutional authority to issue injunctive relief.
No, the NPC has quasi-judicial authority to issue ex-parte CDOs to prevent imminent irreparable harm to data subjects.
Yes, administrative agencies cannot halt commercial processing without 60 days prior notice.
No, but the CDO expires automatically after exactly 24 hours unless affirmed by the Court of Appeals.
items.correct_answer: No, the NPC has quasi-judicial authority to issue ex-parte CDOs to prevent imminent irreparable harm to data subjects.
items.explanation: Under Section 7 of the DPA and NPC Rules of Procedure, the Commission has the statutory authority to issue Cease and Desist Orders motu proprio or upon verified complaint to halt processing that poses grave and irreparable injury to the privacy rights of data subjects.

items.lesson_concept: Judicial Records and Freedom of Information Interplay
items.question_text: A law professor requests copies of an RTC decision regarding a high-profile corporate fraud case to use in a classroom syllabus. The decision contains the names and addresses of witnesses. Under Section 4 of the DPA, how are court records treated?
options: Court decisions are public records and court proceedings are generally accessible, but courts retain discretion to redact SPI or sensitive witness details.
All court decisions are strictly classified as confidential SPI and cannot be shared with academia.
The law professor must secure notarized consent from all parties named in the judgment.
The NPC must inspect and approve the syllabus before the court records can be distributed.
items.correct_answer: Court decisions are public records and court proceedings are generally accessible, but courts retain discretion to redact SPI or sensitive witness details.
items.explanation: Court decisions and judicial records are public documents essential to open justice. However, under Supreme Court guidelines and DPA principles, courts and custodians may redact sensitive personal information (such as victim addresses in sensitive crimes) to balance open courts with privacy.

items.lesson_concept: Legal Weight of NPC Advisory Opinions
items.question_text: A bank relies on an official NPC Advisory Opinion issued to an industry association when designing its cloud backup policy. During a subsequent audit, an NPC compliance officer claims advisory opinions have zero legal significance. What is the correct legal status of NPC Advisory Opinions?
options: They are binding statutory laws equivalent to an Act of Congress.
They constitute authoritative interpretations by the primary regulatory body, establishing administrative guidance that parties may rely upon in good faith.
They are purely academic suggestions that cannot be introduced as evidence in any proceeding.
They only apply to the specific individual who signed the original inquiry letter.
items.correct_answer: They constitute authoritative interpretations by the primary regulatory body, establishing administrative guidance that parties may rely upon in good faith.
items.explanation: NPC Advisory Opinions provide authoritative administrative guidance on the interpretation and application of RA 10173 and its IRR. While not statutes, PICs can cite compliance with official Advisory Opinions as proof of good-faith adherence to regulatory standards.

items.lesson_concept: Mandatory Prior Written Authorization for Sub-processors
items.question_text: A Cloud SaaS provider acting as a PIP migrates its client's customer database to a new subcontractor without the PIC's prior written consent. The contract states 'PIP may optimize technical infrastructure at its sole discretion.' Is the subcontracting valid under the DPA?
options: Yes, generic contractual discretion grants implicit authority to engage sub-processors.
No, engaging a sub-processor strictly requires prior specific or general written authorization from the PIC under the DPA IRR.
Yes, provided the new subcontractor is ISO 27001 certified.
No, only government agencies are forbidden from subcontracting without written consent.
items.correct_answer: No, engaging a sub-processor strictly requires prior specific or general written authorization from the PIC under the DPA IRR.
items.explanation: Section 44 of the DPA IRR mandates that a Personal Information Processor shall not engage another processor (sub-processor) without prior specific or general written authorization of the Personal Information Controller.

items.question_text: A fintech replaces user account numbers with randomly generated UUIDs (hashes), storing the mapping table in an encrypted vault behind multi-factor authentication. Under RA 10173, how is the hashed dataset classified?
options: Completely anonymized data outside the scope of the DPA.
Pseudonymized personal information that remains within the scope of the DPA because re-identification is possible using the key.
Privileged Information by virtue of the encryption vault.
Public domain information since UUIDs contain no alphabetical names.
items.correct_answer: Pseudonymized personal information that remains within the scope of the DPA because re-identification is possible using the key.
items.explanation: Pseudonymization is a security measure that reduces linkability, but as long as a key/mapping table exists that allows re-identification, the data remains Personal Information subject to RA 10173.

items.question_text: A corporate building installs facial recognition turnstiles that convert visitor faces into mathematical vector strings (facial templates) rather than saving JPG photos. What is the precise legal classification of these facial templates?
options: Ordinary personal information because raw photographic images are not stored.
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) under Section 3(l) as biometric data uniquely identifying an individual.
Metadata exempt from data subject notification requirements.
Proprietary software algorithm codes belonging exclusively to the vendor.
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) under Section 3(l) as biometric data uniquely identifying an individual.
items.explanation: Biometric data (including extracted mathematical facial templates, iris scans, and fingerprints) that uniquely identifies a natural person is classified as Sensitive Personal Information under Philippine privacy jurisprudence and NPC advisories.

items.lesson_concept: DPO Independence and No Conflict of Interest
items.question_text: A commercial company designates its General Counsel / Head of Litigation as the Data Protection Officer (DPO). During an NPC audit, the auditor raises an objection. Why does combining DPO and Head of Litigation roles create a potential conflict of interest?
options: Lawyers are legally barred from serving in corporate governance roles.
The Head of Litigation represents the company in adversarial proceedings, whereas the DPO must independently monitor compliance and protect data subject rights without organizational bias.
The DPO must hold an engineering degree recognized by the NPC.
The DPA requires the DPO to always be a full-time third-party external auditor.
items.correct_answer: The Head of Litigation represents the company in adversarial proceedings, whereas the DPO must independently monitor compliance and protect data subject rights without organizational bias.
items.explanation: Under NPC Advisory 2017-01, the DPO must operate independently and avoid conflicts of interest. A Head of Litigation, whose primary duty is defending the company against liability, may face structural conflict when evaluating compliance shortcomings that could expose the firm.

items.lesson_concept: Classification of Ongoing Court Charges and Convictions
items.question_text: A background screening firm logs that an applicant was acquitted of estafa 5 years ago and currently faces an ongoing civil breach of contract suit. Under Section 3(l)(4) of the DPA, how is the record of past criminal acquittal classified?
options: General personal information because an acquittal proves innocence.
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) because it involves an offense committed or alleged to have been committed and the proceeding's disposition.
Public domain data that loses all DPA protection once entered in court books.
Privileged Information between the court stenographer and the judge.
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) because it involves an offense committed or alleged to have been committed and the proceeding's disposition.
items.explanation: Section 3(l)(4) of the DPA explicitly designates as Sensitive Personal Information any information about any proceeding for any offense committed or alleged to have been committed by such person, the disposal of such proceedings, or the sentence of any court in such proceedings.

items.question_text: Company X and Partner Y enter into a Joint Controller partnership to develop an e-wallet. What must they explicitly document in their Joint Controller Arrangement to comply with NPC guidelines?
options: A clause stating that neither party will accept data subject inquiries.
A clear allocation of respective responsibilities for compliance, in particular regarding data subject rights and the designated contact point for users.
An agreement to waive all NPC breach reporting if the breach affects fewer than 5,000 users.
A guarantee that both companies will use identical hardware servers.
items.correct_answer: A clear allocation of respective responsibilities for compliance, in particular regarding data subject rights and the designated contact point for users.
items.explanation: Joint Controllers must determine and document their respective compliance obligations by means of an arrangement, explicitly identifying contact points for data subjects and defining who fulfills specific rights (e.g., access, breach notices).

items.lesson_concept: Marital Status vs Annulment Proceeding Records
items.question_text: An HR portal displays an employee's basic civil status as 'Single' on their corporate badge, while storing their complete court decree of marriage annulment in the confidential personnel archive. How are these two items classified under the DPA?
options: Both are ordinary personal information under Section 3(g).
Both are Sensitive Personal Information under Section 3(l).
Civil status is personal information, while the court decree of annulment containing legal proceedings and psychological findings is Sensitive Personal Information.
Both items become Privileged Information upon notarization.
items.correct_answer: Civil status is personal information, while the court decree of annulment containing legal proceedings and psychological findings is Sensitive Personal Information.
items.explanation: Basic civil status is personal information. However, court decrees of annulment and underlying proceedings involving offenses, health/psychological incapacity, or court dispositions qualify as Sensitive Personal Information under Section 3(l).

tags: Data Protection Officer Designation across Branches
items.lesson_concept: Single DPO for Multiple Related Legal Entities (Group DPO)
items.question_text: A retail conglomerate consists of 12 distinct registered corporate subsidiaries. Can the conglomerate appoint a single Group Data Protection Officer to oversee all 12 entities under NPC Advisory 2017-01?
options: No, every separate SEC-registered legal entity is strictly required to have a distinct, exclusive resident individual DPO.
Yes, a group of companies may appoint a single Group DPO, provided the DPO is easily accessible from each establishment and supported by Compliance Officers for Privacy (COPs).
Yes, but only if all 12 subsidiaries operate within the exact same physical building.
No, Group DPOs are exclusively permitted for foreign multinational entities.
items.correct_answer: Yes, a group of companies may appoint a single Group DPO, provided the DPO is easily accessible from each establishment and supported by Compliance Officers for Privacy (COPs).
items.explanation: Under NPC Advisory 2017-01, a group of related companies may appoint a single DPO (Group DPO) provided that the DPO is easily accessible to all entities, data subjects, and the NPC, typically supported by local Compliance Officers for Privacy (COPs).

items.question_text: To deter theft, a warehouse installs 24/7 audio-recording high-definition CCTV cameras inside employee restrooms and changing cubicles. The company claims 'Legitimate Interest in Asset Protection'. How does the NPC evaluate this surveillance?
options: Lawful, provided visible warning signs are posted outside the restrooms.
A severe violation of Proportionality and reasonable expectation of privacy, rendering the surveillance illegal regardless of employer consent forms.
Permissible if the recorded video files are encrypted with AES-256 and deleted every 7 days.
Valid only if the union leaders signed a collective bargaining agreement agreeing to the cameras.
items.correct_answer: A severe violation of Proportionality and reasonable expectation of privacy, rendering the surveillance illegal regardless of employer consent forms.
items.explanation: Under the Proportionality principle and NPC Advisory 2018-02 on Workplace Surveillance, employees maintain a high and reasonable expectation of privacy in restrooms and locker rooms. Installing surveillance in these areas is intrinsically disproportionate, intrusive, and unlawful.

items.question_text: A mobile banking app only displays its full 30-page Privacy Policy during initial signup. When the app later requests access to the user's phone contacts to enable a 'Send Money to Friend' feature, it displays no explanation. What privacy design practice did the app fail to implement?
options: Data Minimization.
Just-in-Time Privacy Notice explaining specifically why and how contact data is used at the exact moment of permission request.
Annual Security Incident Reporting.
Cryptographic Safe Harbor.
items.correct_answer: Just-in-Time Privacy Notice explaining specifically why and how contact data is used at the exact moment of permission request.
items.explanation: Transparency is not a one-time event. Under Privacy by Design principles, Just-in-Time notices deliver contextual, granular explanations to users at the exact moment sensitive permissions (like address book or microphone access) are triggered.

items.lesson_concept: Incompatible Secondary Processing of Emergency Contact Details
items.question_text: A private university collects emergency contact numbers of students' parents strictly for medical and disaster alerts. The university's commercial auxiliary bookstore uses these numbers to send promotional SMS for back-to-school book sales. Which core principle was breached?
options: Data Portability.
Legitimate Purpose (Purpose Limitation), because commercial marketing is incompatible with the declared purpose of emergency safety.
Accountability through Encryption.
Statutory Reciprocity.
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose (Purpose Limitation), because commercial marketing is incompatible with the declared purpose of emergency safety.
items.explanation: Under Section 11(a) of the DPA (Legitimate Purpose), personal data collected for a specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose (emergency safety) cannot be repurposed for an incompatible secondary commercial objective without obtaining fresh consent.

items.lesson_concept: Retention Limitation and Obligation of Secure Disposal
items.question_text: A telecom retains the complete geolocational call detail records (CDRs) of former subscribers for 25 years after their accounts are terminated, arguing 'storage costs are negligible'. The NTC only requires 1-year retention. Is this compliant with RA 10173?
options: Yes, PICs may store data indefinitely if they have server capacity.
No, Proportionality requires that personal data shall only be retained for as long as necessary for the fulfillment of the declared purpose or legal retention mandates.
Yes, provided former subscribers are sent an annual email confirming their records still exist.
No, all telecom data must be deleted within exactly 24 hours of call termination.
items.correct_answer: No, Proportionality requires that personal data shall only be retained for as long as necessary for the fulfillment of the declared purpose or legal retention mandates.
items.explanation: Under Section 11(e) of RA 10173, personal data must be retained only for as long as necessary for the fulfillment of the declared purposes, or for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims, or as provided by specific law. Retaining granular CDRs for 25 years violates Proportionality.

items.lesson_concept: Transparency in Automated Credit Scoring and Algorithmic Profiling
items.question_text: A micro-lending fintech automatically rejects loan applicants using an AI scoring engine. When rejected applicants ask why they failed, the company replies: 'Our AI is a proprietary black-box trade secret; we cannot provide any explanations.' Does this response comply with Transparency under the DPA?
options: Yes, trade secret laws completely extinguish all privacy disclosure obligations.
No, data subjects have the right to know the existence of automated decision-making, the underlying logic, and the significance and intended consequences of such processing.
Yes, algorithmic transparency only applies to government social welfare programs.
No, but the fintech only needs to show the raw Python source code to the applicant's lawyer.
items.correct_answer: No, data subjects have the right to know the existence of automated decision-making, the underlying logic, and the significance and intended consequences of such processing.
items.explanation: Under Section 16(b) of the DPA and the principle of Transparency, data subjects have the right to be informed regarding automated decision-making, including meaningful information about the logic involved and how profiling decisions affect their rights.

tags: Excessive ID Collection in Building Entry
items.lesson_concept: Data Minimization in Physical Visitor Logs
items.question_text: A commercial office building lobby security officer requires all visitors to surrender their physical passport or PRC license for photocopying and scans their thumbprint before allowing elevator access. Which principle is violated when less intrusive alternatives (e.g., viewing photo ID) suffice?
options: Integrity and Confidentiality.
Proportionality (Data Minimization), because collecting thumbprints and full passport photocopies is excessive for the simple purpose of building security entry.
Extraterritoriality.
Subsidiarity.
items.correct_answer: Proportionality (Data Minimization), because collecting thumbprints and full passport photocopies is excessive for the simple purpose of building security entry.
items.explanation: Proportionality requires processing to be adequate, relevant, suitable, necessary, and not excessive in relation to declared purposes. Retaining photocopies of government IDs and scanning biometrics for casual building visits is grossly excessive.

items.lesson_concept: Freely Given Consent vs Bundled Service Terms (Tying)
items.question_text: A flashlight utility mobile app refuses to turn on the phone's LED light unless the user consents to sharing their real-time GPS coordinates and contact list for third-party advertising. Is this consent legally valid under RA 10173?
options: Yes, users voluntarily chose to download the free application.
No, consent is invalid because it is not freely given and is bundled with a non-essential condition for a basic utility service (tying condition).
Yes, provided the flashlight app discloses the advertising partner names in small print.
No, because mobile apps cannot use advertising as a revenue model in the Philippines.
items.correct_answer: No, consent is invalid because it is not freely given and is bundled with a non-essential condition for a basic utility service (tying condition).
items.explanation: Under Section 3(b) of the DPA and NPC guidance, consent must be freely given, specific, and informed. Bundling non-essential data collection (GPS and contacts) as a mandatory prerequisite to accessing a basic, unrelated service (flashlight function) invalidates the consent.

items.question_text: An online marketplace processes transaction history to prevent fraud and account takeovers without asking for explicit consent every time. Under Section 12(f) of the DPA, what structured assessment must the DPO document to justify Legitimate Interest?
options: A 60-day public notice in the Official Gazette.
A Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA) demonstrating the Purpose Test (legitimate aim), Necessity Test (proportional means), and Balancing Test (fundamental rights of subjects do not override).
A formal waiver approved unanimously by the NPC Commissioners.
An ISO 9001 quality audit certificate.
items.correct_answer: A Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA) demonstrating the Purpose Test (legitimate aim), Necessity Test (proportional means), and Balancing Test (fundamental rights of subjects do not override).
items.explanation: Under Section 12(f) and NPC guidelines, invoking Legitimate Interest requires a documented Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA) addressing: (1) Purpose test, (2) Necessity test, and (3) Balancing test against data subject rights.

items.lesson_concept: Vital Interests Exemption for Sensitive Personal Data under Section 13(c)
items.question_text: An unconscious tourist involved in a severe car crash is rushed to an emergency room. The hospital queries a national blood bank database for the patient's blood type and allergies without their consent. Which lawful basis under Section 13 applies?
options: Section 13(a) Prior Express Consent.
Section 13(c) Protection of Life and Health (Vital Interests), where the data subject is physically incapable of expressing consent.
Section 13(d) Non-commercial processing by a religious organization.
Section 12(b) Fulfillment of a pre-existing commercial contract.
items.correct_answer: Section 13(c) Protection of Life and Health (Vital Interests), where the data subject is physically incapable of expressing consent.
items.explanation: Section 13(c) of the DPA permits processing of Sensitive Personal Information without consent when necessary to protect the life and health of the data subject or another person, and the data subject is physically or legally incapable of expressing consent.

items.lesson_concept: Contractual Necessity vs Forced Consent in Employment
items.question_text: A company requires new hires to submit their SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and bank account details so payroll can disburse salaries. What is the most robust, legally sound lawful basis for this payroll processing under Section 12?
options: Section 12(a) Freely given, revocable consent that the employee can withdraw at any time.
Section 12(b) Processing necessary for the performance of an employment contract and Section 12(c) compliance with statutory legal obligations.
Section 12(e) National emergency declaration.
Section 13(b) Lawful processing by labor unions.
items.correct_answer: Section 12(b) Processing necessary for the performance of an employment contract and Section 12(c) compliance with statutory legal obligations.
items.explanation: Processing employee payroll and statutory remittances is justified under Section 12(b) (contractual necessity) and Section 12(c) (compliance with legal obligation). Relying on consent in an employer-employee relationship is fragile due to the power imbalance.

items.lesson_concept: Section 13(f) Processing for Legal Claims and Court Proceedings
items.question_text: A litigant submits medical records of the opposing party during a personal injury court lawsuit to prove the extent of injuries, without the opposing party's consent. Is this lawful under Section 13(f) of the DPA?
options: No, submitting SPI in court without notarized consent is a criminal offense.
Yes, Section 13(f) authorizes processing of SPI when necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims, or when provided to government/public authorities.
Yes, but only if the litigant obtains a special waiver from the Department of Justice.
No, because only the judge is allowed to look at medical files.
items.correct_answer: Yes, Section 13(f) authorizes processing of SPI when necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims, or when provided to government/public authorities.
items.explanation: Section 13(f) explicitly exempts the processing of Sensitive Personal Information from the consent requirement when necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims, or when provided to government or public authorities in judicial/quasi-judicial proceedings.

items.lesson_concept: Section 13(d) Processing by Religious, Philosophical, and Non-Profit Entities
items.question_text: A church maintains a confidential baptismal and tithing register containing religious affiliation and marriage details of its official members. Can the church share this list with an external political candidate who is a member of the church?
options: Yes, church leadership has absolute discretion over parish records.
No, Section 13(d) strictly restricts processing to bona fide members and prohibits sharing SPI outside the non-profit body without data subject consent.
Yes, because freedom of religion supersedes all privacy laws under the 1987 Constitution.
No, because non-profit organizations are barred from keeping registers of any kind.
items.correct_answer: No, Section 13(d) strictly restricts processing to bona fide members and prohibits sharing SPI outside the non-profit body without data subject consent.
items.explanation: Under Section 13(d), processing by non-profit religious or philosophical associations is permitted for their members, but is subject to the strict limitation that the personal data is not disclosed to third parties without the consent of the data subjects.

items.lesson_concept: Section 12(e) Fulfillment of Constitutional/Statutory Mandate of Public Authorities
items.question_text: The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) audits a taxpayer and orders third-party banks to submit transaction records under the Tax Code. A bank client files an injunction claiming the bank disclosed their data without consent. How should the court resolve the petition?
options: Grant the injunction because the DPA repeals all investigatory powers of the BIR.
Deny the injunction because Section 12(e) permits processing necessary for the fulfillment of the constitutional and statutory mandate of a public authority.
Order the BIR to pay a civil indemnity fee of PHP 1,000,000 to the client.
Hold the bank's DPO in criminal contempt of the NPC.
items.correct_answer: Deny the injunction because Section 12(e) permits processing necessary for the fulfillment of the constitutional and statutory mandate of a public authority.
items.explanation: Section 12(e) of RA 10173 authorizes processing without consent when necessary to fulfill functions of public authority which necessarily includes the processing of personal data for the fulfillment of the mandate of a regulatory agency like the BIR.

tags: Implied vs Explicit Consent for SPI
items.lesson_concept: Strict Requirement for Express, Specific Consent for SPI (Section 13(a))
items.question_text: A wellness clinic includes a pre-checked box in its online form saying 'I consent to the collection and sharing of my medical health records and genetics.' Is this pre-ticked box valid consent for processing SPI?
options: Yes, silence and inactivity constitute valid implied consent under Philippine contract law.
No, consent for Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13(a) must be express, specific, informed, and evidenced by an affirmative, uncoerced opt-in action.
Yes, provided the checkbox is rendered in bold 14pt typeface.
No, but it becomes valid if the user does not submit an objection within 30 days.
items.correct_answer: No, consent for Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13(a) must be express, specific, informed, and evidenced by an affirmative, uncoerced opt-in action.
items.explanation: Under RA 10173 and international privacy standards, consent for SPI must be express, specific, and given through an unambiguous affirmative action. Pre-checked boxes represent opt-out mechanisms and are invalid to establish lawful consent for SPI.

tags: Credit Scoring & Credit Information System Act
items.lesson_concept: Interaction between RA 10173 and Special Laws (RA 9510 CISA)
items.question_text: A commercial bank submits borrower credit data to the Credit Information Corporation (CIC) without securing explicit consent from the borrower. Does the bank violate the DPA?
options: Yes, sharing financial data always requires notarized consent under RA 10173.
No, the Credit Information System Act (RA 9510) mandates submitting basic credit data to the CIC, which is lawful under Section 12(c) (compliance with legal obligation).
Yes, because the DPA automatically repealed all provisions of the CISA in 2012.
No, but the bank must pay a regulatory reporting fee to the NPC for every report.
items.correct_answer: No, the Credit Information System Act (RA 9510) mandates submitting basic credit data to the CIC, which is lawful under Section 12(c) (compliance with legal obligation).
items.explanation: Under Section 12(c) of the DPA, processing is permitted when necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the PIC is subject. The Credit Information System Act (RA 9510) creates a mandatory statutory duty for banks to submit credit data to the CIC.

items.lesson_concept: Mandatory Opt-In Requirements for Electronic Direct Marketing
items.question_text: An online retailer automatically enrolls all users who created an account into receiving third-party telemarketing calls unless they navigate through 5 nested sub-menus to uncheck a toggle. Under NPC Advisory 2018-04, how is this enrollment judged?
options: Lawful under the doctrine of Caveat Emptor.
Unlawful, because direct marketing and third-party data sharing require an affirmative opt-in rather than burdensome, deceptive opt-out dark patterns.
Permissible if the retailer operates on an offshore server.
Valid, provided the calls are conducted between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM.
items.correct_answer: Unlawful, because direct marketing and third-party data sharing require an affirmative opt-in rather than burdensome, deceptive opt-out dark patterns.
items.explanation: Under NPC Advisory 2018-04 and DPA principles, direct marketing through electronic communications requires specific, freely given opt-in consent. Obscuring opt-outs through deceptive UI 'dark patterns' violates Transparency and valid consent standards.

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information vs Sensitive Personal Information (Financial Data)
items.question_text: Under the Philippine Data Privacy Act (RA 10173), what is the statutory classification of an individual's personal bank account number and credit card number?
options: Classified explicitly as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) under Section 3(l).
Classified as Personal Information under Section 3(g), though treated as highly sensitive in risk assessments and cybersecurity safeguards.
Classified as Privileged Information under the Rules of Court.
Public commercial numbers exempt from data protection safeguards.
items.correct_answer: Classified as Personal Information under Section 3(g), though treated as highly sensitive in risk assessments and cybersecurity safeguards.
items.explanation: Unlike some foreign regimes, Section 3(l) of RA 10173 defines SPI as an exhaustive statutory list (race, ethnic origin, marital status, age, color, religious/philosophical/political affiliations, health, education, genetics, sex life, criminal proceedings, government-issued IDs). Bank/credit card numbers fall under Personal Information under Section 3(g), though they demand stringent technical safeguards due to high breach impact.

items.lesson_concept: Redacting Third-Party Personal Data in Access Requests
items.question_text: A customer files a formal Right to Access request demanding a complete copy of an internal dispute resolution ticket. The ticket contains the customer's dialogue along with unredacted home addresses and personal phone numbers of two customer support agents. How should the DPO fulfill the request?
options: Reject the entire request completely under the proprietary trade secret exemption.
Provide the customer's data and dialogue while appropriately redacting the personal identifying information of the support agents to protect their privacy rights.
Release all raw agent data without redactions because the customer's Right to Access is absolute.
Require the customer to obtain a court order before releasing any part of the ticket.
items.correct_answer: Provide the customer's data and dialogue while appropriately redacting the personal identifying information of the support agents to protect their privacy rights.
items.explanation: Under Section 16(c) and NPC guidance, the Right to Access gives subjects access to their own personal data. When a document contains mixed data, the PIC must balance rights by redacting third-party personal data (such as employee home addresses) before disclosure.

items.lesson_concept: Section 18 Scope of the Right to Data Portability
items.question_text: A user switches music streaming providers and invokes Section 18 (Right to Data Portability), demanding their historical listening analytics and playlists. In which technical format must the PIC deliver the data?
options: A printed hard-copy paper binder delivered by registered mail.
In a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable electronic format (such as JSON or CSV) allowing further use by the data subject.
Encrypted binary files that can only be opened with the original provider's proprietary software.
An uncompressed 4K video recording of the user's dashboard screen.
items.correct_answer: In a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable electronic format (such as JSON or CSV) allowing further use by the data subject.
items.explanation: Section 18 of RA 10173 establishes that where personal data is processed by electronic means in a structured format, the data subject has the right to obtain from the PIC a copy in an electronic or structured format that is commonly used and allows further use.

items.lesson_concept: Section 17 Transmissibility of Rights to Heirs and Assignees
items.question_text: A deceased person's bank records are leaked online by a hacker. The deceased person's surviving legal child invokes Section 17 to demand remediation and claim statutory damages. Can the child enforce their deceased parent's data privacy rights?
options: No, privacy rights are strictly personal rights that die completely with the decedent.
Yes, under Section 17, the lawful heirs and assignees of a data subject may invoke the rights of the data subject for which they are an heir or assignee at any time after death.
Yes, but only if the deceased person signed an explicit Power of Attorney before death.
No, only the Solicitor General can represent deceased individuals in privacy matters.
items.correct_answer: Yes, under Section 17, the lawful heirs and assignees of a data subject may invoke the rights of the data subject for which they are an heir or assignee at any time after death.
items.explanation: Section 17 (Transmissibility of Rights) of RA 10173 expressly provides that the lawful heirs and assignees of the data subject may invoke the rights of the data subject for which they are an heir or assignee at any time after the death of the data subject or when the data subject is incapacitated.

items.question_text: A bank client notices their birth date in the bank's core banking database is incorrectly recorded as 1999 instead of 1989 and requests immediate rectification under Section 16(d). What may the bank lawfully require before executing the change across its systems?
options: A non-refundable PHP 5,000 administrative correction fee.
Reasonable documentary verification (such as a certified PSA Birth Certificate or government passport) to substantiate the factual inaccuracy before updating records.
A 90-day waiting period with mandatory account suspension.
Approval signed by the Governor of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.
items.correct_answer: Reasonable documentary verification (such as a certified PSA Birth Certificate or government passport) to substantiate the factual inaccuracy before updating records.
items.explanation: Under Section 16(d) (Right to Rectification), data subjects have the right to dispute and correct inaccuracies. The PIC has a corresponding obligation to ensure data accuracy, which entitles the PIC to request reasonable supporting documentation before modifying critical identity records.

items.lesson_concept: Section 16(f) Right to Damages and Proof of Harm
items.question_text: A telecom accidentally leaks a subscriber's unlisted mobile number to a public forum. The subscriber files a complaint with the NPC solely demanding PHP 5,000,000 in moral and exemplary damages. What is the jurisdictional role of the NPC regarding awarding civil damages?
options: The NPC has exclusive jurisdiction to grant moral damages, taking power away from civil courts.
The NPC may award administrative fines and indemnification under its rules, but formal plenary actions for civil tort damages are adjudicated by regular trial courts (RTCs).
The NPC is legally forbidden from entertaining any complaints involving telecom companies.
The NPC automatically awards PHP 1,000,000 for every leaked phone number without trial.
items.correct_answer: The NPC may award administrative fines and indemnification under its rules, but formal plenary actions for civil tort damages are adjudicated by regular trial courts (RTCs).
items.explanation: Under Section 16(f) of the DPA and Supreme Court jurisprudence, while the NPC investigates violations and enforces administrative penalties/restitution, general civil actions for tortious damages (moral, exemplary) fall under the plenary jurisdiction of regular trial courts.

items.lesson_concept: Interplay between Right to Erasure and Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA)
items.question_text: A bank depositor closes their account and demands the immediate, total erasure of all their financial transaction logs under the Right to Erasure (Section 16(e)). The bank refuses, citing Section 9 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) requiring 5-year retention. How is this conflict resolved?
options: The DPA overrides AMLA because privacy is a fundamental constitutional right.
The bank must comply with the mandatory 5-year statutory retention mandated by AMLA, lawfully overriding the customer's erasure request during that retention period.
The bank must delete 50% of the transactions and keep the remaining 50%.
The bank must pay the depositor an annual storage fee while holding the records.
items.correct_answer: The bank must comply with the mandatory 5-year statutory retention mandated by AMLA, lawfully overriding the customer's erasure request during that retention period.
items.explanation: Data subject rights under Section 16 are not absolute. Under Section 16(e)(1) and Section 19, the Right to Erasure does not apply when the retention of personal data is required by law, such as the mandatory record-keeping requirements under the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

items.lesson_concept: Right to Withdraw Consent and Effects on Prior Lawful Processing
items.question_text: A subscriber consents to biometric processing for facial login on an e-commerce platform. Six months later, they withdraw consent under Section 16(b). What is the legal effect of this withdrawal on the past six months of logins?
options: The past six months of processing retroactively become illegal, and the company must pay damages.
The withdrawal of consent takes effect prospectively from the moment of notice; past processing carried out while valid consent was active remains entirely lawful.
The platform may penalize the user with a breach of contract fine.
The user's account must be permanently deleted immediately across all platforms.
items.correct_answer: The withdrawal of consent takes effect prospectively from the moment of notice; past processing carried out while valid consent was active remains entirely lawful.
items.explanation: Under DPA principles and general legal tenets, withdrawal of consent operates prospectively (ex nunc). It halts future processing based on consent, but does not render prior processing undertaken when valid consent was in force retroactively unlawful.

items.lesson_concept: Penalties for Processing Sensitive Personal Information without Lawful Basis
items.question_text: An unauthorized insider copies and sells 10,000 patient HIV diagnostic records (SPI) on the dark web. Under Section 25(b) of RA 10173 (Unauthorized Processing of SPI), what is the statutory penalty?
options: Community service for 30 days and a written apology.
Imprisonment ranging from 3 to 6 years and a fine of not less than PHP 500,000 nor more than PHP 4,000,000.
A flat administrative fine of PHP 10,000 paid to the NPC.
Permanent suspension of the insider's driver's license only.
items.correct_answer: Imprisonment ranging from 3 to 6 years and a fine of not less than PHP 500,000 nor more than PHP 4,000,000.
items.explanation: Under Section 25(b) of RA 10173, the unauthorized processing of Sensitive Personal Information is punishable by imprisonment ranging from three (3) to six (6) years and a fine of not less than Five hundred thousand pesos (Php 500,000) nor more than Four million pesos (Php 4,000,000).

items.question_text: Under NPC Circular 2022-01 (Guidelines on Administrative Fines), what is the maximum administrative fine that the NPC can impose on a commercial PIC for a grave privacy infraction?
options: A maximum flat rate of PHP 50,000.
Up to five percent (5%) of the annual gross income or gross revenue of the PIC or PIP, or up to PHP 5,000,000, whichever is higher, subject to statutory ceilings.
Up to 50% of the entire net worth of the company.
Zero, because the NPC cannot levy administrative monetary fines without court permission.
items.correct_answer: Up to five percent (5%) of the annual gross income or gross revenue of the PIC or PIP, or up to PHP 5,000,000, whichever is higher, subject to statutory ceilings.
items.explanation: Under NPC Circular 2022-01, the Commission may impose administrative fines ranging from 0.5% to 5% of annual gross income (or revenue), or statutory lump sum amounts up to PHP 5,000,000 per violation depending on gravity, culpability, and mitigating/aggravating factors.

items.lesson_concept: Section 34 Liability of Corporate Directors and Officers
items.question_text: A corporate board of directors knowingly votes to bypass cybersecurity audits to rush an insecure e-commerce platform to market, leading to a catastrophic data spill. Under Section 34 of the DPA, who faces criminal penalties?
options: Only the external software developer who wrote the faulty code.
The penalty shall be imposed upon the responsible directors, officers, or employees who participated in or knowingly permitted the commission of the crime by gross negligence.
The corporation pays a small fee and all directors are completely immune.
The lowest-ranking IT technician on duty during the breach.
items.correct_answer: The penalty shall be imposed upon the responsible directors, officers, or employees who participated in or knowingly permitted the commission of the crime by gross negligence.
items.explanation: Section 34 of RA 10173 establishes that if the offender is a corporation or juridical person, the penalty of imprisonment shall be imposed upon the responsible directors, officers, or employees who participated in or knowingly permitted the commission of the crime through intent or gross negligence.

tags: Section 33 Combination or Series of Acts
items.lesson_concept: Section 33 Combination or Series of Acts Penalties
items.question_text: A criminal syndicate systematically breaks into multiple servers, steals sensitive health records, sells the data, and conceals the breach from authorities. Under Section 33 (Combination or Series of Acts), what is the heightened statutory penalty?
options: Imprisonment of 3 years flat.

Imprisonment ranging from three (3) to six (6) years and a fine of not less than PHP 1,000,000 nor more than PHP 5,000,000 when the offender commits a combination or series of acts penalized under the DPA.
Life imprisonment without parole under the Revised Penal Code.
A simple public warning letter issued by the Department of Trade and Industry.
items.correct_answer: Imprisonment ranging from three (3) to six (6) years and a fine of not less than PHP 1,000,000 nor more than PHP 5,000,000 when the offender commits a combination or series of acts penalized under the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 33 of RA 10173 provides that any person who commits a combination or series of acts including unauthorized processing, access, disposal, and malicious disclosure shall be penalized by imprisonment from 3 to 6 years and a fine from PHP 1M to PHP 5M.

items.question_text: Under NPC Advisory 2017-03, in which scenario is conducting a formal Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) strictly mandatory prior to launching a system?
options: Only when purchasing office stationery supplies.
When a processing system involves automated decision-making/profiling, systematic public surveillance, novel biometric technology, or large-scale processing of Sensitive Personal Information.
When a business has fewer than 5 total employees.
Only when requested in writing by the President of the Philippines.
items.correct_answer: When a processing system involves automated decision-making/profiling, systematic public surveillance, novel biometric technology, or large-scale processing of Sensitive Personal Information.
items.explanation: Under NPC Advisory 2017-03, a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is mandatory whenever processing is likely to result in high risk to the rights of data subjects, such as large-scale SPI processing, biometric matching, mass surveillance, and automated profiling.

items.question_text: Under NPC Circular 2022-04, which threshold automatically triggers mandatory registration of a Personal Information Controller's Data Processing System with the NPC?
options: Employing at least 250 personnel, or processing SPI of at least 1,000 individuals, or processing data likely to pose a risk to rights and freedoms.
Having a paid-up capital of exactly PHP 100,000.
Operating an active social media page with over 500 followers.
Having at least one branch in Metro Manila.
items.correct_answer: Employing at least 250 personnel, or processing SPI of at least 1,000 individuals, or processing data likely to pose a risk to rights and freedoms.
items.explanation: NPC Circular 2022-04 establishes that mandatory registration with the NPC is triggered when a PIC/PIP employs 250 or more persons, or processes sensitive personal information of at least 1,000 individuals, or when processing is likely to pose a risk to rights and freedoms of data subjects.

items.lesson_concept: Cross-Border Data Transfer Safeguards and Accountability Principle
items.question_text: A Philippine corporation transfers its employee records to a parent company's data center in Germany. Under the principle of Accountability (Section 21), what mechanism must the Philippine PIC maintain?
options: The Philippine PIC must use contractual or other reasonable means (e.g., Cross-Border Data Sharing Agreements / Standard Contractual Clauses) to ensure recipient compliance with comparable privacy safeguards.
The Philippine company is immediately relieved of all legal accountability the moment data crosses international airspace.
All international data transfers are strictly illegal under Section 21.
The Philippine PIC must require the German government to sign a bilateral peace treaty.
items.correct_answer: The Philippine PIC must use contractual or other reasonable means (e.g., Cross-Border Data Sharing Agreements / Standard Contractual Clauses) to ensure recipient compliance with comparable privacy safeguards.
items.explanation: Section 21 of the DPA (Principle of Accountability) establishes that the PIC remains accountable for personal data under its control, including data transferred to third parties abroad. The PIC must use contractual or other reasonable means to provide a comparable level of protection.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Circular 16-03 Tripartite Mandatory Breach Notification Rule
items.question_text: Under NPC Circular 16-03, mandatory notification to both the NPC and affected data subjects within 72 hours is required only when which three conditions concur simultaneously?
options: The breach affects at least 1,000,000 users, causes financial bankruptcy, and is broadcast on national television.
(1) Sensitive Personal Information or financial data is involved, (2) there is reasonable belief of unauthorized acquisition, and (3) the breach poses a real risk of serious harm to data subjects.
The breach occurs on a weekend, involves ordinary names only, and the DPO was on vacation.
The hacker demands a ransom exceeding PHP 100,000,000 in Bitcoin.
items.correct_answer: (1) Sensitive Personal Information or financial data is involved, (2) there is reasonable belief of unauthorized acquisition, and (3) the breach poses a real risk of serious harm to data subjects.
items.explanation: Under Section 38 of the IRR and NPC Circular 16-03, mandatory breach notification to the NPC and data subjects is triggered when all three criteria are met: (1) SPI or other information that may enable identity fraud, (2) unauthorized acquisition, and (3) real risk of serious harm.

items.lesson_concept: Computation of the 72-Hour Breach Notification Timeline
items.question_text: A cybersecurity team detects suspicious server traffic on Friday night and definitively confirms on Saturday morning that an attacker exfiltrated 5,000 patient credit card and health records. When does the 72-hour notification clock start ticking?
options: On the following Monday morning when official government offices open at 8:00 AM.
From the moment of knowledge or reasonable belief that a personal data breach has occurred (Saturday morning confirmation).
Only after the company finishes its final forensic root-cause analysis report 30 days later.
From the date when the affected customers first discover the leak on social media.
items.correct_answer: From the moment of knowledge or reasonable belief that a personal data breach has occurred (Saturday morning confirmation).
items.explanation: Under NPC Circular 16-03, the 72-hour notification clock begins from the moment the PIC obtains knowledge or reasonably believes that a security incident has occurred that satisfies the mandatory notification criteria.

items.question_text: A laptop containing an encrypted database of 20,000 employee records is stolen from a manager's car. The database is encrypted using industry-standard AES-256 and the decryption key is securely held on a separate hardware security module (HSM). Must the DPO notify the affected employees?
options: Yes, notification is always mandatory whenever any physical computer is stolen.
No, the Encryption Safe Harbor applies because the encrypted data is completely unreadable and unusable to unauthorized third parties without the key.
Yes, but only if the stolen laptop was valued at more than PHP 50,000.
No, but the company must buy every employee a new laptop as compensation.
items.correct_answer: No, the Encryption Safe Harbor applies because the encrypted data is completely unreadable and unusable to unauthorized third parties without the key.
items.explanation: Under Section 38 of the DPA IRR and NPC Circular 16-03, notification to data subjects is not required if the personal data was protected by effective technological measures (e.g., robust AES-256 encryption where the key was not compromised), rendering the data unreadable to unauthorized persons.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Circular 16-03 Full Breach Report Extension Protocol
items.question_text: A DPO timely submits the preliminary 72-hour notification via the NPC DBNMS portal. Complex external digital forensics will take another 20 days. How must the DPO manage the standard 5-day Full Breach Report deadline?
options: Refuse to communicate with the NPC until all forensics are 100% complete.
Submit a written request for extension within the initial period detailing the technical complexity and providing interim progress updates as findings emerge.
File a motion to dismiss the breach investigation at the Court of Appeals.
Fabricate preliminary findings to satisfy the 5-day deadline.
items.correct_answer: Submit a written request for extension within the initial period detailing the technical complexity and providing interim progress updates as findings emerge.
items.explanation: Under NPC Circular 16-03, while a Full Breach Report is due within five (5) days from the initial notification, the PIC may request an extension for justifiable technical reasons, provided the request is made before the lapse of the deadline and includes interim findings.

items.lesson_concept: Data Breach Notification Management System (DBNMS) Mandate
items.question_text: Under NPC Advisory 2022-01, what is the mandatory official channel through which registered PICs and PIPs must file their Annual Security Incident Reports (ASIR) and Data Breach Notifications?
options: Direct message to the official NPC Facebook page.
The NPC Data Breach Notification Management System (DBNMS) online portal.
A hand-delivered paper letter stamped at the nearest Post Office.
An unencrypted plain-text email sent to the Privacy Commissioner's personal inbox.
items.correct_answer: The NPC Data Breach Notification Management System (DBNMS) online portal.
items.explanation: NPC Advisory 2022-01 mandates the exclusive use of the Data Breach Notification Management System (DBNMS) web portal for submitting preliminary breach notifications, full reports, and the mandatory Annual Security Incident Report (ASIR).

items.lesson_concept: Law Enforcement Delay of Data Subject Breach Notification
items.question_text: The Philippine National Police Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) determines that immediately notifying data subjects about an active server compromise will alert the criminal hacker and destroy evidence in an ongoing sting operation. How can subject notification be lawfully deferred?
options: The DPO can unilaterally decide never to notify the subjects.
The law enforcement agency must submit a formal written certification requesting the NPC to authorize a temporary postponement of notification to data subjects.
The DPO can only delay notification if the President signs an executive order.
Police requests have zero legal effect and notification can never be delayed under any circumstance.
items.correct_answer: The law enforcement agency must submit a formal written certification requesting the NPC to authorize a temporary postponement of notification to data subjects.
items.explanation: Under Section 38(c) of the IRR and NPC Circular 16-03, notification may be postponed upon the formal written request of a law enforcement agency or when the Commission determines that notification would compromise criminal investigations or national security.
